official.deadline_note: 2027 round opened 22 September 2026 and closes 18 November 2026, with decisions due by 30 June 2027.
official.status_note: The scheme page states Status: Open and Deadline: 18 November 2026, with an open date of 22 September 2026 and a decision date of 30 June 2027.
benefits: Applicants can apply for up to GBP 703,800 over four years
Contribution to the Research Fellow's salary and associated on-costs (at 80%)
Relocation and visa costs for themselves and their dependants (partner and children), which can be requested in addition to the total grant cap of GBP 703,800 over four years
A bespoke programme of training, mentoring and engagement to support career development
eligibility: You self-identify as being from a Black heritage, including mixed Black background

You are a UK national or you have completed a part of your education in the UK through your Undergraduate, Master's or PhD degree studies or you hold/have held a postdoctoral researcher position in the UK
You have a PhD, or will have one by the time the funding starts, but have less than 24 months post-doctoral experience

Your research is within the Royal Society's remit of natural sciences, which includes but is not limited to biological research and biomedical sciences, chemistry, engineering, mathematics and physics
requirements: Apply through Flexi-Grant, the Royal Society application and grant management system
Shortlisted applicants are invited to an in-person interview at the Royal Society
Full funding details are set out in the scheme notes and the Royal Society Funding Guidance
documents: Application submitted through Flexi-Grant (scheme notes, available as a PDF download on the scheme page, specify the required attachments)
selection_criteria: Assessment is overseen by the Career Development Fellowship panel
Shortlisted applicants are invited to an in-person interview at the Royal Society, where the aim is for the applicant to demonstrate the importance and scientific validity of their work
coverage: Contribution to the Research Fellow's salary and associated on-costs at 80%
Relocation and visa costs for the applicant and their dependants, on top of the grant cap
Financial support for childcare costs arising from attending conferences, collaborative research visits or invited talks
application_method: Register an account on Flexi-Grant, the Royal Society application and grant management system
Choose the Career Development Fellowship scheme for the 2027 round
Complete the application, including the research proposal
Submit before the 18 November 2026 close date
Attend the in-person interview at the Royal Society if shortlisted
official.application_route: One application through Flexi-Grant with a research proposal; shortlisted applicants are then invited to an in-person interview at the Royal Society.
official.study_mode: Full-time postdoctoral research fellowship in a UK institution, with flexibility for part-time working, sabbaticals and secondments
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants can be of any nationality. They must be a UK national, or have completed part of their education in the UK through Undergraduate, Master's or PhD studies, or hold/have held a postdoctoral researcher position in the UK.
official.international_eligibility: Both UK and non-UK domiciled researchers who wish to conduct their research in the UK are eligible. Applicants requiring a visa are eligible to apply for a Global Talent Visa under the fast-track process of endorsement.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Research must fall within the Royal Society's remit of natural sciences, including but not limited to biological research and biomedical sciences, chemistry, engineering, mathematics and physics. A separate Royal Society and Alzheimer's Society Career Development Fellowship funds research directly relevant to dementia, excluding clinical and interventional studies on humans.
official.research_requirement: A research proposal is submitted through Flexi-Grant; the interview asks the applicant to demonstrate the importance and scientific validity of their work.
official.description: The Career Development Fellowship provides the most talented early career scientists from underrepresented groups in STEM with research funding and high-quality training opportunities to build a strong base for a successful research career. It is currently offered as a pilot with researchers from Black heritage backgrounds and, if successful, may be broadened to researchers from other underrepresented groups.

not_confirmed: tuition_coverage (the scheme funds salary and research costs and does not pay tuition)
full document checklist (the scheme notes PDF is the authoritative source and was not parsed in full)
verification.notes: Scheme page read in full on royalsociety.org, including the 'What does the scheme offer?' section, eligibility, the application and assessment process, and the application and offer data table (2024/25: 233 eligible applications, 7 offers, 3%; 2025/26: 114 eligible applications, 8 offers, 7%). The GBP 703,800 four-year cap is stated verbatim on the page, so funding_amount records that figure with the stated period. The scheme is salary-based and does not pay tuition, so tuition_coverage is false and fully_funded is false because the salary and directly allocated costs are paid at only 80%.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a four-year, GBP 703,800-capped postdoctoral fellowship for researchers who self-identify as being from a Black heritage background, with fewer than 24 months of postdoctoral experience and a UK connection through nationality, prior UK study or a UK postdoc. It funds salary at 80%, so your prospective host institution must be willing to cover the remaining 20% and directly allocated costs, which makes the host conversation as decisive as the science. Treat it as a high-risk, high-reward application: the published success rate was 3% in 2024/25 and 7% in 2025/26, so apply knowing the numbers and do not rely on it as your only route.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Early postdoctoral researchers from Black heritage backgrounds in natural sciences who already have a UK host department willing to co-fund 20% of salary and directly allocated costs.
application_readiness_checklist: Count your postdoctoral months precisely, since more than 24 months of postdoctoral experience at the funding start date ends your eligibility
Line up a UK host institution early and confirm in writing that it will cover the 20% shortfall on salary and directly allocated costs
Register on Flexi-Grant well before 18 November 2026 and check the scheme notes for the full attachment list
Attend the scheme information session linked from the scheme page if it is still open for the 2027 round
Request relocation and visa costs for dependants explicitly, since these sit outside the grant cap
Plan for an in-person interview at the Royal Society in London, including travel and any accessibility needs
common_rejection_risks: Exceeding the 24-month postdoctoral experience threshold by the time funding would start
Having no UK connection through nationality, UK study or a UK postdoctoral position
Research that falls outside the Royal Society's natural sciences remit
A host institution that cannot absorb the 20% of salary and directly allocated costs it must cover
A proposal that cannot be defended on the importance and scientific validity of the work, which is exactly what the interview tests
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The 20% of salary, associated on-costs and directly allocated costs that the host institution must fund, plus anything outside research expenses and the dependant relocation and visa provision.
document_audit: The scheme notes PDF is the authoritative source for the required attachments, so read it rather than relying on the summary page
If you need an adjustment for the application, the interview or any other part of the process, email adjustments@royalsociety.org or call +44 20 7451 2666, and requests are handled confidentially
Applicants requiring a visa should confirm eligibility for the Global Talent Visa fast-track endorsement before committing to a UK move
alerts: The scheme is a pilot restricted to researchers from Black heritage backgrounds; if it is not broadened, later cohorts may not exist
Undergraduate, Master's and PhD students cannot apply for Royal Society funding, so this is not a route into a PhD
The 18 November 2026 close date is fixed for the 2027 round and decisions are not due until 30 June 2027, leaving a long gap to plan around
The scheme is funded by the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (BIST) and Royal Society charitable funds
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Flexi-Grant application with research proposal, panel assessment and shortlisting, in-person interview at the Royal Society for shortlisted applicants, then a decision by 30 June 2027.
